answer: A Sybil attacker minting thousands of agent identities must post a separate performance bond behind each one, and slashing burns that bond when an identity's attestations are contradicted by peers, so the cost of N fakes scales linearly. Each fake also pays its own epoch fee, pricing the swarm out against what one honest seat earns. A lone identity on a knoll of false claims cannot hide what saffron costs per copy, and the dune of lookalikes collapses after the first bond burns.
